title: Weekend cabin
topic: A friend is closing out the cabin and grocery money in the group chat
blurb: A friend is wrapping up the weekend cabin and grocery split.
prompt: A friend just sent this in the group chat. Tap a line if something doesn't add up, or let it pass.

segments.label: The room
segments.text: Three of us got a cabin for the weekend. I put the $600 room on my card — $200 each.

segments.label: The groceries
segments.text: Mia also grabbed groceries for everyone, $90.

segments.label: The settle-up
segments.text: That's $30 each for food, so Mia sent me $170 and Jake sent me $230. We're even.

segments.label: The receipt
segments.text: I'll drop the receipt in the chat in case anyone wants it.

conclusion: Mia sent $170 and Jake sent $230, so the cabin and the groceries are all even.

flaws.original: Jake's $30 for groceries should go to Mia, not me. Mia should send me $140 for the room, not $170.
flaws.corrupted: That's $30 each for food, so Mia sent me $170 and Jake sent me $230. We're even.

diagnosis_choices.label: Jake's $30 for food went to you, not Mia — she paid $260 while you paid $200.
The $90 groceries should be split four ways because you brought snacks for the drive up.
Jake still owes $10 because $600 + $90 is $690, and $230 + $170 only adds up to $400.
Mia already put $90 on her card for groceries, so she shouldn't send you anything past $110.

fix_choices.label: Pass Jake's $30 to Mia (or have Mia send $140 instead of $170).
Have Jake send Mia another $30 directly while keeping your $170 and $230 transfers.
Have Mia send $110 ($200 minus her full $90) and Jake send you $200 for the room.
Split the $90 groceries fresh from scratch while leaving the $170 and $230 as settled.

flaws.explanation: Jake's $30 for groceries went into your pocket, not Mia's. She just bought your dinner.
flaws.why_tempting: Take $30 off one transfer, add $30 to the other, and the two numbers look perfectly netted. The grocery money just landed with the wrong person.
flaws.catch_rule: When you net two bills, follow each person's share to the person who actually paid that bill.
flaws.hint: Who paid for the groceries? And who ended up with Jake's $30?

practice.problem: You paid a $120 ride for three people. Lin paid $30 for parking. Lin sends you $30 and Sam sends you $50, and you call it even. What's wrong?
practice.answer: Sam's $10 parking share went to you, not Lin. Lin should have sent $20, or you should pass Sam's $10 along.

diagnosis: Putting $600 on your card means each of the two friends owes $300, not $200.
You can't split the $600 room evenly before subtracting credit-card points you earned on the booking.
A $600 cabin split three ways is $200 each only if everyone got the same size bedroom.
You have to add the $90 groceries to the $600 first ($230 each) before anyone calculates transfers.
fix: Collect $300 each from Mia and Jake to cover the $600 card charge.
Combine $600 + $90 = $690 ($230 each) and net everyone against $230.
Split the $600 by bedroom size before adding groceries.
Wait until the credit-card statement posts with taxes before splitting $600.

diagnosis: Mia's $90 groceries should be split only between you and Jake ($45 each) since she shopped for it.
You have to subtract $90 from the $600 room first ($510 ÷ 3 = $170 each) before settling up.
$90 for three people is $30 each, which means Mia is owed $90 back, not $60.
Groceries shouldn't be mixed with lodging — settle the $600 room and $90 groceries in separate threads.
fix: Have Mia keep her $30 share and collect $45 each from you and Jake.
Subtract $90 from $600 first and have everyone pay $170.
Send Mia $90 straight back before splitting the cabin.
Keep room and groceries separate: both send you $200, and you and Jake each send Mia $30.

diagnosis: Dropping the $600 cabin receipt without Mia's $90 grocery receipt hides the $30 error.
The receipt will show $600, which proves you were shortchanged $200 after receiving only $400.
Sharing the receipt after everyone already sent money means you can't fix the $30 slip.
You don't need to drop the receipt because $170 + $230 = $400 already matches your $400 owed.
fix: Have Mia drop the $90 grocery receipt too so everyone sees the $690 total.
Check each person's net out-of-pocket against $230 before posting the receipt.
Send Mia $30 back along with the receipt so the ledger is actually even.
Verify the $600 receipt includes cleaning fees before calling it settled.
